A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same thermally activated dual-modal adversarial clothing study. All pages, equations and ten figures are readable and comparable. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix; both refer to separate supplementary videos.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original digital attack comparisons and physical clothing experiments, including activation, temperature, viewing-angle and distance results.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the original digital attack comparisons and physical activation and robustness experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same layered garment, thermal activation mechanism and two-stage shape-then-texture optimization, including EOT and total-variation/average-precision losses. Revised supporting citations do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both use INRIA, PennFudan, FLIR and LLVIP and the same indoor, shopping-mall and outdoor scenarios. v3 explicitly adds PennFudan and FLIR to the Section 4.2 description, but both already appear in v1's settings and Figure 6.

E2.justification: Figure 6 retains the visible baselines T-SEA, AdvYOLO, CAP, FDA, AdvTexture and AdvCloak, and infrared baselines AdvIC, AdvIB, AIP, HIC-IR and Bulb. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same four detectors, pretraining/fine-tuning setup, patch placement and area constraint, top-ten selection for fabrication, and ASR definition with a 0.5 detection threshold. No evaluation setting is revised.

E4.justification: The activation-time, temperature, thermal-hysteresis and angle/distance analyses in Section 5 and Figures 8–10 are unchanged. Figure 7 also retains the same physical case studies.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains identical error bars. Neither version explains their statistical meaning or supplies run counts or seeds; no uncertainty-reporting or significance-testing procedure is added.

E6.justification: The plotted results, physical examples and temperature curves are unchanged. Section 4.2 repeats the same numerical results, including LLVIP ASRs of 85.4%, 88.6%, 83.3% and 80.2%; the activation and effectiveness-boundary findings are also retained.

T1.justification: Equation (1), the paired-image and detector definitions, and the ASR formula are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contribution and claims of controllable dual-modal evasion, including the abstract's 50-second activation and above-80% success-rate claims. Removing a redundant introductory summary does not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations involving polygonal geometry and thermal hysteresis, and the same applicability boundaries: reduced visible-spectrum effectiveness beyond 30 m and demonstrated angular robustness within 35 degrees. No substantive limitation or interpretation is added.

D1.justification: The dye preparation and supplier, heating-pad specifications, camera and resolution, and garment dimensions remain unchanged. No new implementation settings, code/data access instructions or resource release is documented.

R1.justification: v3 expands citations with works such as Shape Matters, PhysPatch and natural-looking clothing textures, and changes the citations supporting the optimization losses. The related-work discussion and positioning remain largely unchanged; the bibliography also duplicates REAP.

P1.justification: v3 adds two authors, fuller affiliations, contact information and funding acknowledgments. It makes localized wording edits and removes a redundant introductory sentence, while retaining the section structure and nearly all scientific prose.

P2.justification: All ten figures retain the same visual evidence. Figures 1 and 10 are resized, captions receive small edits, and the expanded author and reference blocks cause layout reflow. No experimental figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The expanded citations and fuller description of Figure 6 provide small documentation benefits, while the scientific evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These benefits are balanced by minor editorial defects, including duplicate REAP references [21]/[22] and 'video demoxx' in Section 3.2. Overall quality remains essentially unchanged.
